data.body:
RCA / disposition evidence (current origin/main 92bfc4d3919072daa85fbd5664489d3b95693bd0):

Observation: the heartbeat canary was accurately stale. `gh run list --workflow reconcile-bridge.yml --limit 10` showed the last reconcile-bridge success was run 33971771591, created 2026-09-05T14:25:29Z and completed 2026-09-05T14:33:52Z. The latest canary failure before intervention was run 34150470717 at 2026-09-07T18:09:08Z with log `::error::Reconciler is stale — Reconciler unhealthy — canonical status is STALE.`

Hypothesis: the bridge was not failing inside reconcile/Jira/acli; it had been manually disabled, so no scheduled bridge runs were being created. Confirmation: `gh workflow list --all | grep -E 'Reconcile Bridge|Reconciler Heartbeat'` reported `Reconcile Bridge disabled_manually` while the canary was active. The latest pre-stale bridge log (run 33971771591) ended successfully with `BRIDGE_STATE: converged` and `Published rebar/host:bridge_run_failures=0`, ruling out a reconciler/acli/Jira runtime failure for the stale window.

Action/confirmation: re-enabled and dispatched the workflow with `gh workflow enable reconcile-bridge.yml` and `gh workflow run reconcile-bridge.yml --ref main --field mode=live` (run 34152772338). That run completed success at 2026-09-07T19:10:29Z; its log includes `BRIDGE_STATE: converged` and `Published rebar/host:bridge_run_failures=0`. Then dispatched the heartbeat canary (run 34155415169), which completed success at 2026-09-07T19:27:58Z; its stale-fail step was skipped. Current `gh workflow list --all` reports `Reconcile Bridge active`.

Conclusion: root cause was operational workflow disabled_manually; addressed by re-enabling and proving a successful bridge run plus a green canary. No repository code change was required.
